phase: ## Phase 2: MP3 copies in the wrapper
summary: Pass, with no Blocker, no Major, and no new finding. Commit 2b29c067 closes F5 and F6, the adversarial tests of 81511930 close F7, and the log correction in d7ca282e closes F8. The 136 checks of the r3 probe passed on the committed wrapper, and the 117 committed tests passed. Each of 28 wrapper variants fails at least one committed test and at least one probe check, and none survives. HEAD is two commits after the audited commit, and those commits change no audited path. A2 is not applicable, and A6 shows no overstatement.
evidence: Provenance: `git rev-parse HEAD` printed d7ca282ebd6e7602420096055266f527d2f9ff7f at the start of the audit, and this value is role_base_sha and audited_head_sha. Near the end HEAD was cb7e911ba12bb3cf934815e584ab645fae45517e, two commits later, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor d7ca282e HEAD` exited 0. Both new commits (7cb58934 and cb7e911b) belong to track asset_chibi_sprouts_r1_20261022 and change only assets/sprout-lily.ts, one run log, and one plan. `git diff --quiet d7ca282e HEAD -- scripts tests sounds measure/tracks/audio_game_integration_20261014 measure/runs/audio_game_integration_20261014 measure/tracks.md measure/generated` exited 0, so each audited path is equal at both commits. `git diff --quiet HEAD -- scripts tests sounds measure/tracks/audio_game_integration_20261014` also exited 0 for the working tree. The phase_base_sha 16b398b595354f5da275268f1b32c8e864b9312a resolves to a commit.

Applicability: `git diff --name-status a1b67c77..d7ca282e` lists seven paths. Two are code: scripts/sound-set.mjs (M) starts two programs and removes files, and tests/sound-set.adversarial-p2.test.ts (A) runs the wrapper. The other five are records: measure/backlog.md, measure/index.md, green-p2.log, the plan of this track, and the plan of another track. The test strategy marks Phase 2 as `Applicable, reduced: argv, no shell` for Review B (test-strategy.md:405), so the role stays applicable.

Delta scope: `git show --stat` shows that 2b29c067 changes only scripts/sound-set.mjs (14 insertions, 13 deletions). It shows that 81511930 adds only the test file (265 lines). It shows that d7ca282e changes only green-p2.log and plan.md. The AC2 argv and the AC2 failure lines are unchanged. Probes P1, P2, and P6 confirm both.

F5 closed: scripts/sound-set.mjs:90-94 skips each PATH entry that `isAbsolute` rejects, so `.`, `bin`, `./bin`, and `..` never supply a binary. Probe P4.relativeEntry ran those four entries, and each run exited 1 with the exact `ffmpeg not found` line and zero ffmpeg calls. For each entry, `bash` resolved `command -v ffmpeg` to the planted file (`./ffmpeg`, `bin/ffmpeg`, `./bin/ffmpeg`, `../ffmpeg`), so the oracle shows that the planted file would have run. A relative entry ahead of a real absolute entry left the planted file unused and ran the real binary (P4.relativeEntry.dotBeforeRealBinary). Red's tests `F5 never searches the explicit relative PATH entry` for `.` and `bin` pin the rule. The r2 wrapper fails all five probe cases and those two tests, and mutants M23 and M24 fail 8 and 2 tests.

F6 closed: scripts/sound-set.mjs:79-82 applies `isExecutableFile` (a regular file with the execute bit) to the resolved EARSHOT_BIN before any preparation. Probe P4.earshot.closed ran nine failing values. They are an empty value, a folder, a non-executable file, /dev/null, and a dangling link. They also include a link to a folder, a link loop, a path of 5,000 characters, and a FIFO. Each run exited 1 with the exact `earshot not found at <resolved path>` line, made zero earshot and ffmpeg calls, and kept both old files.

F6 closed, order and success cases: a rejected earshot path creates no output folder (P4.earshot.noOutputFolder), and the earshot line comes before the ffmpeg line (P4.earshot.checkedBeforeFfmpeg). A link to an executable file and a relative path with a slash still run (P4.ok.earshotSymlinkToExecutableFile, P4.ok.earshotRelativePathWithSlash). The r2 wrapper fails 8 probe checks, among them the earshot case with an empty value, and Red's two F6 tests fail on it.

F7 closed: tests/sound-set.adversarial-p2.test.ts (81511930) holds 19 tests, and they pin the two rules of F7. Six tests cover an empty PATH entry (empty, leading, trailing, middle, only separators, and an empty entry ahead of a real candidate). Two tests cover a non-executable file as FFMPEG_BIN and as a PATH candidate. Mutant M23 (no absolute-entry check) fails 8 tests. Mutant M4 (no execute-bit check) fails 4 tests. In r2, the analogous variants M2 and M4 kept 98 of 98 tests green, and M2 no longer applies, because 2b29c067 replaced its anchor line.

F8 closed: green-p2.log:114 now reads `5 failed, 93 passed (98)`, and green-p2.log:173 records the correction. The numbers match red-p2.log:92 and my r2 run of mutant M21, where the tests part gave `5 failed | 93 passed (98)`.

Process start: scripts/sound-set.mjs calls `spawnSync` twice (earshot at :135, ffmpeg at :146). Each call passes a program path and an argv array and sets no `shell` option. The file imports no exec, eval, or vm API (probe P0). Probe P2 used FFMPEG_BIN and EARSHOT_BIN names with `;`, `$()`, backticks, quotes, `&`, `|`, `<`, and `>`. All 8 runs exited 0, created no marker file, and sent the AC2 argv to ffmpeg. A copy with `shell: true` on ffmpeg (mutant M10) created marker files, failed 6 probe checks, and failed 21 tests.

Names: the name rules (SAFE_NAME for the set and each entry) are unchanged in this delta. Probe P3 (20 invalid entry names and 9 invalid set arguments) passed again. Each run ended with the exact `bad name` or `bad set name` line, zero earshot calls, and no new file. A loosened name check (mutant M11) wrote files outside `sounds/fake`, failed 27 probe checks, and failed 15 tests. Names such as `--help` and `-x` pass the check, but ffmpeg receives absolute paths, so no name becomes an option.

Lookup stays closed (r1 F1). Probe P4 passed again with 15 failing lookups, 7 lookups that must work, and 5 empty-entry checks. A failed lookup exits 1 with the exact `ffmpeg not found` line, makes zero earshot calls, and creates no output folder. The lookup runs once, before the output folder exists and before any target preparation.

Preparation stays closed (r1 F2): probe P5 passed again. Its cases are blocked `.ogg` and `.mp3` targets, six links at the two targets, an unwritable folder, and a set folder that is a file. A blocked target exits 1 with the exact `cannot prepare output` line and keeps the stale files of that entry. The preparation lines (scripts/sound-set.mjs:113-133) are unchanged in this delta. After a failed ffmpeg run the new `.ogg` stays and the old `.mp3` is gone, so a stale MP3 cannot pass the post-check (INFO P5.failedFfmpeg.state). A symlinked output folder is followed, as before this phase (INFO P5.outDirSymlink), and the caller owns that link.

MP3 files: probe P1 ran the wrapper with the default PATH lookup, the real ffmpeg 8.0.1-3ubuntu2, and a stand-in earshot that copies the committed Ogg. The run exited 0, wrote 14 files, and printed the 15 expected lines. The seven MP3 files have the same SHA-256 as the committed files. Probe P1b found no tag line and none of the tested markers in them (71136 bytes in 7 files). Probe P8 gave four bad Ogg inputs, and each ended with `ffmpeg failed` and no MP3 file.

Error output: probe P6 ran seven failure scenarios with a canary value in the environment. Two more checks pin the exact `ffmpeg failed` and `ffmpeg wrote no file` lines. No line held the canary or an environment value of 12 characters or more. The wrapper echoes only the FFMPEG_BIN value that the caller set. It prints earshot output after a successful render, as before this phase, and it never prints ffmpeg output (INFO P6.successEcho).

Observation, no finding: a one-off run outside the probe used `EARSHOT_BIN=earshot-bare`, a name without a slash. The committed wrapper and the r2 wrapper both read it as a path in the working directory, because both call `resolve()` (scripts/sound-set.mjs:79 and a1b67c77:67). With a copy on PATH only, the committed wrapper exits 1 with `earshot not found at <cwd>/earshot-bare`, runs nothing, and creates no output folder. With one copy in the working directory and one on PATH, only the working-directory copy runs, the file that the guard checked. A variant that spawns the raw value runs the PATH copy instead, and no committed test or probe check uses such a name. The default path is absolute, so I record no finding.

Observation, no finding: explicit paths stay the choice of the caller. A relative FFMPEG_BIN path with a slash runs the named file (P4.ok.relativePathWithSlash). An absolute PATH entry that names the working directory (`/proc/self/cwd`) is searched (INFO P4.absoluteEntry.procSelfCwd). The comment at scripts/sound-set.mjs:84 names only an absolute path and a basename. The claim of plan.md:163 that the working directory is never searched holds for the PATH lookup.

Observation, no finding: empty values and a trailing slash. An empty EARSHOT_BIN fails closed, and the line names the working directory, the form that Red's test pins. An empty FFMPEG_BIN is unset, so the two variables differ by design. A trailing slash on an earshot file path is removed by `resolve()`, so the named file runs (INFO P4.earshot.trailingSlashOnFile).

Targeted tests: the five Phase 2 test files through heavy-run.sh gave 5 files passed and 117 of 117 tests passed (4.52 s). The count equals the 98 tests of r2 plus the 19 tests of 81511930, and it matches plan.md. After the run, `git status --short -- sounds scripts tests measure/tracks/audio_game_integration_20261014` printed nothing, and the SHA-256 over sounds/ is 68f9a40e4e5f60898e21899b0edd5f8707c6be4bbb304b285ed71e7a5a2e8376, equal to the r1 and r2 value. The new test file creates its fixtures under `~/.cache/opencode/sound-set-adversarial-p2-*` and removes them, and none remains. No `/tmp/review-b-*` folder remains. The old folder `~/.cache/opencode/sound set adversarial Y9gOA4` from an earlier round remains, and no new folder appeared.

Mutation run, tests: the five committed test files ran in a temp tree against 28 variants of the wrapper, through heavy-run.sh. The unchanged copy (M0) gave 117 passed. All 28 variants fail at least one test, and none survives. Of the 28, 25 are mutants of the committed wrapper. Two replay older wrappers (M21 is 6804d082 and M22 is a1b67c77), and one is a design variant (M30). M22 fails four tests: two for F5 and two for F6.

Failed tests per variant, lookup group: M1 (bare name checked in the working directory) 8; M3 (folder accepted) 6; M4 (no execute-bit check) 4. M5 (empty FFMPEG_BIN not unset) 1; M6 (no ffmpeg guard) 16; M20 (PATH loop never runs) 6; M23 (no absolute-entry check) 8. M24 (relative entries honored, the r2 rule) 2; M28 (ffmpeg check after preparation) 15. Earshot group: M25 (access-only guard) 2; M26 (no guard) 4; M27 (guard after preparation) 2. M29 (guard ignores the execute bit) 1; M30 (empty value means the default) 1; M31 (value not resolved) 1.

Failed tests per variant, other groups. Preparation group: M7 (no pre-check of the targets) 1; M8 (`.mp3` target not prepared) 2; M9 (no post-check of the MP3 file) 1. Encode and name group: M10 (`shell: true` on ffmpeg) 21; M11 (loosened name check) 15; M12 to M17 (one dropped ffmpeg flag each) 2 each. Replays: M21 (the 6804d082 wrapper) 17; M22 (the a1b67c77 wrapper) 4.

Mutation run, probe: the r3 probe ran directly (`--probe-only`) against the same 28 variants, because the probe is light. The unchanged copy (M0) gave 136 of 136. The probe fails at least one behavioral check (a check other than P0) on every variant. The probe sees every variant that the tests see. It sees M30 and M31 through P4.earshot.closed.empty.

Behavioral failures per variant follow in three parts. Part 1: M1 9; M3 6; M4 3; M5 1; M6 26; M7 2; M8 5; M9 1; M10 6; M11 27. Part 2: M12 12; M13 21; M14 12; M15 21; M16 12; M17 12; M20 23; M21 21; M22 8; M23 10. Part 3: M24 5; M25 3; M26 11; M27 11; M28 23; M29 3; M30 1; M31 1.

r2 mutants file, rerun on the new wrapper (tests part, four files): M0 gave 98 passed. M2, M18, and M19 report MUTATION DID NOT APPLY, because 2b29c067 replaced their three anchor lines. M18 and M19 were my candidate fixes of F6 and F5. The 18 variants that still apply all fail 1 to 17 tests. M4, the r2 survivor, now fails 1 test, because the earshot guard shares `isExecutableFile`. M21 (the 6804d082 wrapper) still gives `5 failed | 93 passed (98)`, the number of F8.

Probe lineage: the r3 probe holds every check id of the r2 probe (118 ids) and adds 18, 136 in all. The 18 are five relative-entry cases, nine earshot cases, two checks for earshot order and output folder, and two earshot success cases. The r2 probe on the committed wrapper gave 117 of 118. The one failure is its static check P0.hardeningLinesPresent, which looks for the old `dir === ''` line. The r1 probe gave 79 of 79 on the committed wrapper. Six r1 ids carry a new name since r2: P4.a.absentPath, P4.d.nonExecutableFile, P4.e.bareNameNotOnPath, P4.h.pathUnsetNoFfmpeg, P4.k.relativePathWithSlash, and P5.mp3IsDirectory.failsClosed.

A2: not applicable. `git diff a1b67c77..d7ca282e --text -- scripts tests sounds | grep -n -i -E 'published|draft|consent|anonymi'` printed nothing, so the delta holds no draft-to-published flip. Secret scan: the added lines of the range printed nothing for these patterns. The patterns are api key, secret, bearer, password, credential, authorization, token, private-key headers, e-mail addresses, and IPv4 addresses.

A6: `git diff --stat a1b67c77..d7ca282e -- measure/tracks.md measure/index.md` shows only measure/index.md (1 insertion). The registry line measure/tracks.md:71 only links the track, so the registry claims no security state. The plan uses `resolved` and `resolves` only for the ffmpeg lookup (plan.md:131 and :162). Its claim `Adversarial F5 and F6 are fixed` (:177) matches the green adversarial file (117 of 117 tests). My mutants M22, M24, M25, M26, M27, M30, and M31 fail the F5 or F6 tests, so those tests bite.

Prod wiring: the default earshot path .venv-earshot/bin/earshot is a regular executable file (`-rwxrwxr-x`, 260 bytes). The check `statSync().isFile()` plus `accessSync` with X_OK returned true for it. So the new guard accepts the production default. package.json holds no script that names sound-set.

Helper files: keep review-b-d7ca282-probe.mjs (136 checks) and review-b-d7ca282-mutants.mjs (28 variants and a control; modes `--tests-only` and `--probe-only`). Both read the repository and write only to mkdtemp folders under /tmp, which they remove. The four older helper files can go: review-b-a1b67c7-probe.mjs, review-b-a1b67c7-mutants.mjs, review-b-6804d08-probe.mjs, and review-b-6804d08-mutants.mjs. The r3 probe holds every check id of the r2 probe, and six r1 ids carry a new name. The r3 mutants file replays the r1 wrapper as M21 and the r2 wrapper as M22. The orchestrator removes the four files, because the role shell denies rm; the r1 and r2 JSON and log files stay as records.

Limits: I did not run the real earshot render, the project-wide gate, tsc, or measure/doctor.sh, because Green and Review A own those results. I checked process, path, and metadata safety, not audio quality. A file with `chattr +i` was not tested, because it needs root. The one-off run for the name without a slash is not saved as a file.
Not tested, for a later track: the AC2 argv pins no input format and no protocol list. So ffmpeg would parse untrusted media if a downloaded take replaced a set file.

Independence and CONTEST: I did not read the Review A result files, which exist untracked in the same folder. No CONTEST item reached Review B in this round. The brief states that adversarial testing confirmed F5 and F6 as blockers, and I do not contest that statement. Both findings are closed in code, in tests, and in my probe and mutants.
